newsitem.title: UK: Albanian leader cannot guarantee aid convoy safety.
newsitem.headline: Albanian leader cannot guarantee aid convoy safety.

text.p: Albanian leader Sali Berisha said in an interview published on Tuesday that he could not guarantee the safety of humanitarian aid convoys sent to help the population of his impoverished anarchic Balkan state.
The European Union said on Monday it would not object to individual countries sending troops to Albania as military escorts for aid convoys but shied away from organising its own multinational force.

The EU estimates that Albania needs $10 million in basic medical supplies as well as 10,000 tonnes of flour. Albania wants foreign police units to help secure ports, airports, roads and railways to ensure the safe distribution of relief supplies.
"I could not say that international convoys would be safe on our territory for the moment, and they must have full security," Berisha told the Times newspaper.

An Italian air force transport plane flew in six tonnes of emergency medical aid for the country on Monday for the northern part of the country, which is under government control. It sent two tonnes of medical aid for the rebel-held south over the weekend.

The EU has already turned down an Albanian request for large-scale military intervention to help restore order after rebels looted weapons from army depots and rose against Berisha, blaming him for failed savings schemes that bankrupted thousands.
